plan.detail: Fort Wayne Open, 2017: Laleh took the van keys from Coach Dunleavy's bag, and the four she left behind each paid $61 for a Greyhound seat home

opener.text: Seven. Eight. Twenty-two dollars a seat up there, kids. That's about a dollar a second.
Six. Seven. Somebody tell the Mole she got paid by the round and only worked one and a half.
Eight. Nine. Hold onto your stubs. Those are worth more now than they were at the door.
Five. Six. Her whole purse comes to about forty dollars a minute tonight. Write that down.

personal.text: Sixty-one dollars for a Greyhound seat out of Fort Wayne, and she billed me for it every year for nine years. I just settled it in one minute forty-seven.
Your coach told you about the van. Four seats, sixty-one apiece, two hundred forty-four dollars. That's the most she ever charged anybody, and she charged me.
Dunleavy kept the Greyhound receipt in his gear bag to show me what I owed. She trains in his old gym now and that receipt is still the most she ever earned.
She rode nine hours on a sixty-one-dollar ticket from Fort Wayne so she'd have something to tell you about me. That was the best investment she ever made. Tonight it stopped paying.

closer.text: I'm not staying for the reading. I don't work overtime.
Keep the change, Mole. I'll take the van.
Dunleavy said this belt was worth more than she was. Turns out he had the number right.
Your next lesson with her should cost less. Ask for a discount.
